name: Rasuwa flood
where: Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and downstream, Nepal
headline: Rasuwa flood, live
lede: A flash flood came down the Bhote Koshi from Tibet into Rasuwa on 26 August 2026. Here is what is confirmed, what is still unknown, and who to call.
asOfSource: Nepal Police, reported by ABC News

stats.label: confirmed dead
stats.detail: Nepal Police raised the toll to 547 in a Friday evening bulletin, reported by ABC News, coming within minutes of Nepal's disaster authority, NDRRMA, putting the figure at 538. Nepal Police also reported 1,473 people injured in Nepal, up from 466 the day before. Earlier steps: 489 at midday Friday, 469 at 7am the same day and 389 the previous evening. The last full district breakdown, from Friday's midday bulletin, summed to 489: Chitwan 186, Nawalparasi East 112, Gorkha 44, Dhading 40, Nuwakot 37, Tanahun 29, Nawalparasi West 28, Rasuwa 13; no bulletin since has restated district figures against the new total. Sources differ on whether 547 counts deaths on the China side, where state media separately raised their own toll to 5 on Friday, so they are not added here.

stats.label: listed missing in Nepal
stats.detail: NDRRMA put the figure at 977 people out of contact in a Friday morning update, up from 910 the evening before, 517 of them foreign nationals, reported by IANS. This figure is NDRRMA's, not the police's. Out of contact does not mean dead: phone lines, power and internet are still down across the valley.

stats.label: missing on the China side
stats.detail: Chinese state media report 558 people missing around Gyirong Port in Xizang (Tibet), 260 of them foreign nationals. Combined with Nepal's list that is more than 1,300 people unaccounted for, although the two countries' counts of foreign nationals may overlap.

stats.label: rescued so far
stats.detail: NDRRMA reports 113 people rescued from Timure, Dhunche, Syabrubesi, Uttargaya and Bidur: 88 Nepali citizens, 11 Indian, 8 Chinese, 4 Korean and 2 American. The authority has published their names. Nepal Police separately reported 1,545 people rescued in total as of its 7am bulletin on 28 August, reported by Onlinekhabar. NDRRMA itself told ABC News on Friday afternoon that 3,253 people have now been rescued by helicopter across the flood zone, a still broader tally that has not been named or broken down. The Nepali Army said its helicopters had rescued 706 people by 3pm Friday, up from 449 at 12:20pm, including 40 foreign nationals (29 Indian, 4 German, 4 Chinese, 1 Omani and 2 South Korean), reported by Onlinekhabar. Nepal Tourism Board separately said 117 stranded tourists have been rescued from the Bhotekoshi area, reported by Onlinekhabar.

stats.label: hydropower projects damaged
stats.detail: The Nepal Electricity Authority reports 14 projects damaged with a combined capacity of about 748 MW: 9 operating plants (354 MW) and 5 under construction (394 MW). Named ones include Rasuwagadhi, Chilime, Sanjen Khola, Upper Trishuli-1, Trishuli and Devighat, plus a 220 kV substation. An earlier same-day Ministry of Energy estimate said 431 MW.

stats.label: since the flood
stats.detail: Counting from the morning of 26 August 2026, when the flood hit. Search, rescue and recovery work is still going on this many days later.

stats.label: damage, early estimate
stats.detail: Physical Infrastructure Minister Sunil Lamsal put damage to roads and bridges at about Rs 200 billion on 26 August, and called it preliminary. Hydropower and private property are not in that figure. The whole 42 km road from Betrawati to the Rasuwagadhi border crossing was destroyed at multiple points.

stats.label: relief money released
stats.detail: Rs 1 billion released by the government into the disaster relief fund, plus Rs 10 million each to Rasuwa and Nuwakot and Rs 5 million to Dhading. Public donations are not counted here until an official total is published.
